correctness.rationale: For unit Fock kernels at z_j=√(ρN)exp(2πij/N), direct Fourier transform of their normalized circulant Gram gives exactly λ_{N,k}=N P(Poisson(ρN)≡k mod N), which is positive. The maximum is √(N/(2πρ))(1+O_ρ(1/N)) by Poisson local Stirling and exponential separation. For 0<ρ≤e^-1, unimodality and endpoint ratio p_0/p_{N−1}∼ρ√(2πN)exp[N(−1−logρ)] show unique minimizing Fourier residue N−1 even at threshold, giving λ_min=√N/(ρ√(2π)) exp(−N(ρ−1−logρ))(1+O_ρ(1/N)). For ρ>e^-1, the strictly increasing φ(u)=(u+1)log(u+1)−u logu gives unique u>0 satisfying φ(u)=1+logρ, so I_ρ(u)=I_ρ(u+1)=H>0, u<ρ<u+1. Convexity localizes globally least residues to integers Nu+O_ρ(1); two Poisson aliases at Nu+δ and N(u+1)+δ have prefactor a^δ/√u + b^δ/√(u+1), δ∈Z−{Nu}; strict convexity reduces D_N minimization to two nearby integers. Uniform Stirling and remote-alias exponential gaps yield stated O_ρ(1/N) and squared κ. Independent log-sum-exp Poisson-residue comparisons for N=80,160,320 and ρ∈{0.2,e^-1,0.45,1,2} gave log-asymptotic discrepancies ≤0.0042. Finite checks corroborate, do not prove all N.
